added_failures_note: derived from the reviewed run's own arm logs on disk: logs/baseline.log names revision 720736d7f8 (51 passed, EXIT=0, no FAILED line) and logs/after.log names revision 9004a30e8d (52 passed, EXIT=0, no FAILED line), so the set difference is empty (0). The separate importer arm is not the armed suite pair; its single head failure (tests/test_a_slow_station_still_reads_as_alive.py::test_a_blocked_tick_keeps_a_fresh_beat_and_reads_slow, logs/importers-after.log, EXIT=1) cleared on both repeats at the same head (logs/importers-after-rerun.log, 64 passed, EXIT=0) and its base arm passed (logs/importers-base.log, 64 passed, EXIT=0); it is recorded as a non-blocking finding rather than counted as an added failure.
call_sites: reckon/crew/station.py:890 (run_forever's loop calls station.tick()); Station constructed at reckon/crew/station.py:866

findings.text: the module docstring carries incident dates (12-13 November) and changelog prose ('The tick used to commit a project's transitions ...' at :5), which the naming rules ban in source comments and docstrings; it should state the mechanism (a derivation held open must not delay another project's commit) and leave the incident narrative to the evidence fragment and commit message.

the two passes both run in the tick's own thread, so a slow derivation still delays the NEXT tick's transitions by up to the derivation's duration; the deliverable's 'independently of it, so a slow derivation never delays a phase event' therefore holds within a tick but not across ticks, and the 44-58 minute derivation the plan describes would still delay transitions taken during it until the following tick starts.

test_logs records no ruff check or ruff format --check result although the done_when names both on the staged paths; I ran them at head and both are clean, but the worker's own record does not carry the fact it was told to produce.

baseline_suite and after_suite use the keys result/exit/log rather than the contract's exit_status/completed/failure_count/failure_ids/log_path, so the run's classification parsed every one of those fields as null and a promotion reader may read the arms as unreadable even though the logs themselves are complete.

retry_failures records only the new case's four red runs; the importer arm's head failure and its rerun to green are absent from that field, so a reader relying on retry_failures alone would not learn that a matched arm went red before the recorded green.

the log opens with the pytest progress line rather than the '# revision:' and '# command:' headers the done_when requires of each arm's log, so the mutation it records cannot be re-run from the log alone; it does end in a bare EXIT=1 with the expected FAILED id.
